subject: CloudStream replacement: StreamFast onboarding and EU transit impact
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudstream.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 18:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Notice: CloudStream -> StreamFast subcontractor change (impact to EU traffic)

Hi Ben and Marissa,

Quick note to let you know CloudStream will be migrating our streaming ingestion and edge processing to a newly acquired partner, StreamFast, starting June 1. This affects the CDN/edge collector we currently list as a CloudStream-managed subprocessor.

What we are sharing now: a CSV mapping of the updated vendor roster and the new data flow (attached: cloudstream_streamfast_subprocessor_matrix.csv). High level: StreamFast will handle short-lived telemetry and metric batching; they will not persist raw customer payloads beyond 72 hours.

Key items for BrightHealth:
- Data residency: StreamFast operates EU POPs and will keep EU-origin traffic within EU by default.
- Access controls: StreamFast integrates with CloudStream's KMS; they do not have direct read access to decrypted user content.

We'd like confirmation from Redwood on whether this change needs a DPA amendment or any additional evidence for EU customers. Happy to hop on a call next week.

Attachments: cloudstream_streamfast_subprocessor_matrix.csv

Best,
Alice
Director, Compliance Operations
CloudStream
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudstream.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: CloudStream -> StreamFast subcontractor change (impact to EU traffic)

Thanks for the heads up, Alice — and for the CSV. I skimmed it and a few quick questions:

1) Is StreamFast a named subprocessor in CloudStream's DPA now, or will that be included in a future roster update/notice?
2) Can you confirm whether StreamFast will ever perform decryption of payloads for debugging (i.e., support access to plaintext) or only process encrypted blobs?
3) For our EU customers like BrightHealth we need a clear description of cross-border flows (if any). The CSV shows EU POPs but I want the canonical statement we can pass to legal.

Marissa — can you pick this up for review with Legal? If it looks like a material change we may need a DPA addendum and a BrightHealth notification.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudstream.io>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: CloudStream -> StreamFast subcontractor change (impact to EU traffic)

Ben + Alice — I pulled the CSV and flagged the rows where StreamFast has access to aggregated telemetry vs. any PII-derived fields. A few clarifications we need before internal sign-off (and before BrightHealth gets notified):

- Explicit statement on encryption-at-rest keys: who holds the KMS keys for the ephemeral store? (CloudStream or StreamFast?)
- Retention enforcement: you mentioned 72h for raw payloads — is that configurable per customer or globally enforced? We need to know if BrightHealth can request a shorter retention window in writing.
- Subprocessor liability: will CloudStream accept the same indemnities/contractual obligations with respect to data subject requests and exports that are in your current DPA?

Naomi — looping you in for legal review. If you can draft a short addendum template or confirm whether the current DPA's catch-all notices suffice, that would be ideal.

Marissa
Head of Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudstream.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:28:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Notice: CloudStream -> StreamFast subcontractor change (impact to EU traffic)

Thanks — answers inline below and attaching a short questionnaire we filled out (redwood_questionnaire_answers.pdf):

- Named subprocessor: StreamFast will be added to the published subprocessor roster on May 25. We will send a formal notice and DPA addendum if our legal review requires it.
- KMS/keys: CloudStream retains KMS control. StreamFast will process only encrypted blobs. Decryption is performed inside CloudStream's staging environment under strict audit, and only for on-call debugging by authorized engineers. Those sessions are logged and time-limited.
- Retention: 72 hours is the global default for the ephemeral store. It is configurable on an enterprise plan level; customers can request shorter retention by signing an addendum (we can include language).
- Liability: CloudStream will accept the standard subprocessor obligations that are in your DPA; we will include StreamFast in that scope and mirror the same commitments.

Let us know if you want a redline for a one-off addendum for BrightHealth. We can also schedule a short sync with their legal team to walk through controls.

Attachments: redwood_questionnaire_answers.pdf

Best,
Alice
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@cloudstream.io>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: CloudStream -> StreamFast subcontractor change (impact to EU traffic)

Thanks Alice — that helps. Quick internal notes and next steps for BrightHealth:

- Draft: I'll prepare a short DPA addendum we can use as a template for customers who require explicit naming of subprocessors. It will state StreamFast is subprocessor for streaming ingestion/edge processing and include retention, encryption, and export clauses.
- Evidence: Please send the StreamFast SOC-type attestation (if available) or an internal control summary for their EU POPs. If they don't have a formal SOC yet, a security questionnaire + network diagram is fine.
- Customer notification: For BrightHealth, given their sensitivity, we should schedule a 30-min call next week to present the addendum and the controls. Ben — can you coordinate the invite with Tom Becker at BrightHealth?

If CloudStream can provide the attestation by EOD May 20 that will give us time to prepare the addendum.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
